skill.name: competitor-customer-finder
skill.description: Find companies named in a competitor's public customer logos and case studies. Use Leadsets to match company domains to buyer roles and return ranked contacts with source links and email status.
skill.summary: Find contacts at publicly named competitor customers and trace each account to its source.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: All 28 static alerts are false positives: they match Markdown, documented service URLs, or routine research instructions. Leadsets is a disclosed external dependency, and no direct prompt injection was found in the reviewed source. Separate concerns include untrusted scraped content, spreadsheet exports, and transfers of contact data.

remediation.issue: Untrusted web content enters the agent workflow
remediation.suggestion: Treat scraped pages and tool results as data only. Validate extracted company names and domains before using them in tool calls.
Write external values as literal text in Sheets. In CSV exports, neutralize formula-like cell values, including values with leading whitespace or control characters.

remediation.issue: Connector exports lack a separate review step
remediation.suggestion: Preview the contact rows and confirm the destination, access permissions, and fields before writing to an external connector. Use a vetted destination with automations disabled.

content.value_statement: Competitor customer names are often scattered across logos and case studies. This skill links those accounts to source pages and finds contacts that match your buyer roles.
actual_capabilities: Collect customer names from public logos and case studies and retain a source URL for each account.
Match company names to domains using links on those pages and list unresolved names separately.
Search Leadsets for contacts by domain, function, title, and seniority.
Rank contacts by role match and seniority, and group them by reported email status.
Check available quotas and report search records and scrape units used.
Return a CSV by default or write to a chosen destination using a connected tool.
limitations: Scraping requires a paid Leadsets plan with scrape units and is not available on the free plan.
It only reads public pages and does not guess companies or domains missing from the source pages.
A public logo or case study does not confirm that a company is still a customer.
It does not enrich or verify emails itself, write outreach, or send messages.

use_cases.title: Research a competing product
use_cases.description: Review the accounts a rival names in public and use the source links to check its presence in your market.

use_cases.title: Find relevant buyers at named accounts
use_cases.description: Find a short list of contacts in a chosen function at each identified account.

use_cases.title: Build a reviewable account list
use_cases.description: Combine results across competitors, deduplicate domains, and review unresolved names before importing the list.

prompt_templates.title: Start with one competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Find customers publicly named on [competitor domain]. Find up to two operations leaders at each resolved account and return a CSV.
prompt_templates.scenario: First search with one competitor and one buyer function.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on specific roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [competitor domain] for public customer logos and case studies. Find up to three heads or directors of sales operations per account and include the source URLs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Research with a defined role and seniority.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Find publicly named accounts for [domain A] and [domain B]. Deduplicate by customer domain and keep the source links for both competitors. Find two finance leaders per account.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a verified-only shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Leadsets quotas before researching [competitor domains]. Test the RevOps role filters with one result before running the full search. Return up to three contacts with verified work emails per customer. Include unresolved accounts and usage counts in the CSV.
prompt_templates.scenario: A constrained run with quota checks and an email status filter.

output_examples.input: Find two operations leaders per publicly named customer on a sample competitor site.
output: Illustrative result: The CSV lists six contacts across four accounts.
Each account entry includes its customer domain, a source page, and the evidence type.
Two contacts have verified work emails, one is catch-all, and three are unconfirmed.

output_examples.input: Research a sample competitor that names several companies but does not link to all of them.
output: Illustrative result: The report lists two accounts with resolved domains and matching contacts.
Three customer names appear in the unresolved section with their source pages.
No domains were guessed for those companies.

best_practices: Specify the buyer function, seniority, and maximum number of contacts per account.
Check each source page before treating a public mention as evidence of a current relationship.
Review a CSV first and confirm access permissions before exporting contact data to a shared destination.
anti_patterns: Treating a public logo as proof that an account still uses the competitor.
Labeling catch-all or unconfirmed email addresses as verified.
Exporting names and email addresses to a shared or automated destination without reviewing the rows and permissions.

faq.question: What setup do I need?
faq.answer: Connect the Leadsets MCP server to your agent or use a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Can I run this on the free plan?
faq.answer: No. The workflow stops if the account is on the free plan or has no scrape units available.

faq.question: Where do the customer names come from?
faq.answer: Names come from the competitor's public pages, such as customer logo lists and case studies. Each account includes the page that names it.

faq.question: What happens when a customer domain is missing?
faq.answer: The name goes into an unresolved list with its source page. The skill does not guess a domain.

faq.question: Does the skill verify email addresses?
faq.answer: No. It reports available email status and keeps catch-all and unconfirmed contacts separate from verified contacts.

faq.question: Where can I put the results?
faq.answer: The default is CSV. A connected Google Sheets, CRM, or sequencer tool can be used as a destination.
